ayahOccurrences.text: وَٱسْتَبَقَا ٱلْبَابَ وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُۥ مِن دُبُرٍ وَأَلْفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَا ٱلْبَابِ ۚ قَالَتْ مَا جَزَآءُ مَنْ أَرَادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوٓءًا إِلَّآ أَن يُسْجَنَ أَوْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ

ayahOccurrences.text: وَقَالَ لِلَّذِى ظَنَّ أَنَّهُۥ نَاجٍ مِّنْهُمَا ٱذْكُرْنِى عِندَ رَبِّكَ فَأَنسَىٰهُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِۦ فَلَبِثَ فِى ٱلسِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ

lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: يُسْجَنَ is in the derivative form: يَسْجُن
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
س/ج/ن   s–j–n prison, imprisonment, confinement, detention. Philologists who derive the Qur’anic word سِجيِّن sijjın from this root suggest ‘containment’ as the semantic link between the two, but it has also been suggested that it could be a borrowing from Latin ‘insignia’, the Roman emperor’s stamp which used to be affixed to important records. Also it has been suggested that this root was borrowed from Persian or Ethiopic.

Of this root, 5 forms occur 12 times in the Qur’an:
يَسْجُن yasjun 1 time;يُسْجَن yusjan 2 times; مَسْجونين masjūnın 1 time; سِجْن sijn 6 times andسِجيِّن sijjın 2 times.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
يَسْجُن yasjun [imperf. of v. trans.; pass. v. يُسْجَن yusjan] to imprison, to detain

(12:35) ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا الآيَاتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ حَتَّى حِينٍ but it occurred to them, [even] after seeing the evidence [for his innocence], that they should imprison him for a while.

entries.label: سِجّين
entries.definitionHtml:
سِجّين sijjın [n.] a written record enumerating the bad deeds of the wicked

(83:7–9)‏إِنَّ‏ ‏كِتَابَ‏ ‏الْفُجَّارِ‏ ‏لَفِي‏ ‏سِجِّينٍ‏ ‏وَمَا‏ ‏أَدْرَاكَ‏ ‏مَا‏ ‏سِجِّين كِتَابٌ مَرْقُومٌ ‏the list of the wicked is in Sijjın, what will explain to you what Sijjın is?–a clearly numbered list.

entries.label: مَسْجونين
entries.definitionHtml:
مَسْجونين masjūnın [pl. of pas. part. masjūn] one imprisoned

(26:29) لَئِنِ اتَّخَذْتَ إِلَهًا غَيْرِي لأََجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ الْمَسْجُونِينَ if you take any god other than me, I will make you among the prisoners.
